s.g: The mast below the topgallant mast in a square-rigged ship.
(constellation) An autumn constellation of the northern sky whose brightest three stars form a small triangle. It lies near Perseus, between Aries and Andromeda.
(anatomy) A bladder, especially the urinary bladder or the gall bladder.
A province, particularly (historical) the first-level administrative divisions of the Ottoman Empire.
The office, position, rank, or title of a voivode (“a local ruler or official in various parts of central and eastern Europe; an administrative chief in modern Poland”).
(historical) An ancient nomadic-based people that formed a state or confederation north of the agriculture-based empire of the Han dynasty.
A group of matriculation exams taken in the final year of German secondary school. [from mid 20th c.]
A native or inhabitant of Andorra; a person of Andorran citizenship or nationality and their descendants. [from 1823]
(biochemistry, genetics) Any subsequence of nucleic acid, selected from a large random sequence-pool, used to bind to a specific target molecule.
A broom made from a bundle of twigs tied onto a shaft.

Molecules, such as amino acids, sugars, nucleic acids, proteins, polysaccharides, DNA, and RNA, that occur naturally in living organisms; any such molecule, even if created outside a living thing (as for example in a test tube or bioreactor).
Any of several forms of butylene.
The study of dialects.

a freshwater lake in the north-west European part of Russia, located on the territory of Republic of Karelia, Leningrad Oblast and Vologda Oblast
Capable of being opened.

Any of very many vines, in North America and elsewhere, of the genus Passiflora that bear edible fruit called passion fruit, and showy flowers of a structure symbolic of the Passion of Christ.

Semiotics, the study of signs.

Someone from, or pertaining to Chuvashia
To take the virginity of (somebody), especially a woman or girl.
